record.context_brief: Severe ill-posedness with only limited kernel smoothness
record.original_question: Let A map L2(0,1) into an arbitrary Hilbert space Y, assume A is a Hilbert-Schmidt operator with non-closed range, and let k in L2([0,1] x [0,1]) be the kernel of A* A: L2(0,1) -> L2(0,1). If k has limited smoothness, meaning that k is not infinitely many times continuously differentiable on the whole closed unit square [0,1] x [0,1], under what conditions can the operator equation Ax = y nevertheless be severely ill-posed, in particular exponentially ill-posed?

evidence.quote: Open Question 3: Under which conditions can an operator equation (4) with a Hilbert-Schmidt operator A mapping from L2 (0, 1) into an arbitrary Hilbert space Y with non-closed range R(A) be severely (exponentially) ill-posed in the sense of Definition 1, provided that the kernel k in L2 ([0, 1] x [0, 1]) from A* A : L2 (0, 1) -> L2 (0, 1) has limited smoothness, which means that k is not infinitely many continuously differentiable on the whole closed unit square?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Y$ be an arbitrary Hilbert space and let $A : L^2(0,1) \to Y$ be a Hilbert–Schmidt operator whose range $R(A)$ is non-closed in $Y$. Then the composition $A^*A : L^2(0,1) \to L^2(0,1)$ is a self-adjoint, non-negative, Hilbert–Schmidt integral operator with a (symmetric) kernel $k \in L^2([0,1]\times[0,1])$, i.e.
$$(A^*A x)(s) = \int_0^1 k(s,t)\, x(t)\, dt, \qquad s \in [0,1].$$
Call the linear operator equation $Ax = y$ severely (exponentially) ill-posed if the singular values $\sigma_n(A)$ of $A$ decay to zero exponentially fast as $n \to \infty$, i.e. there exists $c>0$ such that $\sigma_n(A) = O(e^{-cn})$.

Suppose the kernel $k$ has only limited smoothness, in the sense that $k$ is not infinitely many times continuously differentiable on the whole closed unit square $[0,1]\times[0,1]$.

Find conditions on $k$ (equivalently on $A$) under which the equation $Ax = y$ can nevertheless be severely, in particular exponentially, ill-posed. In other words, characterize the kernels $k \in L^2([0,1]\times[0,1])$ of limited smoothness for which the singular values of the associated Hilbert–Schmidt operator $A$ decay exponentially.
artifact.category_tag: Ill-posed inverse problems / Hilbert–Schmidt integral operators
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the inverse-problems literature concerning the relationship between kernel smoothness of a Hilbert–Schmidt operator and the exponential decay of its singular values. A follow-up note by Hofmann–Hofmann (2022) and related work indicate that no general analytical criterion is known that links limited smoothness of the kernel k to exponential ill-posedness; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A note on open questions asked to analysis and numerics concerning the Hausdorff moment problem
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of open questions concerning severe ill-posedness and kernel smoothness of Hilbert–Schmidt operators; no conclusive analytical link established.
status_evidence.claim: The question of when limited kernel smoothness still allows exponential ill-posedness is still considered open.

status_evidence.title: On the Degree of Ill-posedness for Linear Problems with Noncompact Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses degree of ill-posedness for linear operator equations in Hilbert spaces and relations between smoothing properties and singular value decay.
status_evidence.claim: Background showing that the precise relationship between kernel smoothness and exponential singular value decay is not fully resolved.
